title: Bug: signing-key must be a valid hexadecimal string
question:
**Describe the bug**
Upgrading from `v1.8.2` (or `v1.8.3-beta.1`) to any newer version seems to cause Inngest to throw the following error during initialization, even though the signing key is correctly set. 
```
inngest-1  | Error: signing-key must be a valid hexadecimal string
inngest-1 exited with code 1
```


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Follow the self hosting instructions from the docs
2. Use `inngest/inngest:v1.8.3-beta.1` and the following service setup (I'm duplicating the env vars for explicitness)
```
    image: inngest/inngest:v1.8.3-beta.1
    command: 'inngest start'
    ports:
      - '${INNGEST_PORT_FORWARD}:8288'
      - '${INNGEST_PORT_FORWARD_CONNECT}:8289'
    environment:
      - INNGEST_EVENT_KEY=eventkey
      - INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY=signingkey
```
4. Run your services with `docker compose up`
5. Inspect the logs and confirm that  inngest is up and running as expected
6. Now upgrade your inngest image to `1.9.0` and rerun the services
7. You should now see the following error:
```
inngest-1  | Error: signing-key must be a valid hexadecimal string
inngest-1 exited with code 1
```

**Expected behavior**
I expect that the Inngest server correctly reads the signing key from the environment.

**System info**
- OS: x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Version: >=1.9.0

**Additional context**
Happy to provide more details if needed :)
gold_answer: The signing key must be a valid hexadecimal string. The validation was added because non-hex keys were not being signed correctly, so the error is intentional. Generate a key as described in the self-hosting docs configuration section (for example, `openssl rand -hex 32`).
gold_thread:
Hi there, we recently discovered that signing keys that were not hexadecimal strings weren't correctly signed so this new error is a new valid warning to ensure that when folks are setting signing keys, hexadecimal keys are used. 

The recently updated docs provide a simple way to create a key: [https://www.inngest.com/docs/self-hosting#configuration](https://www.inngest.com/docs/self-hosting#configuration)

title: Function fails if output is larger than 1MB
question: **Describe the bug** The output of my function is quite big (> 1MB). It made the function fail but I don't think that should be the right behavior. When the output is > 1MB, we handled this case by not displaying the output but allow it to be downloaded: https://github.com/inngest/inngest/pull/650 The error I see in my case: ``` Body exceeded 1mb limit ``` **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start inngest: `npx inngest-cli@latest dev` 2. Start a function that return large output (1MB) **Expected behavior** The function should complete even when the output is too large, instead of failing **Screenshots / Stack trace dump** **System info** - inngest-cli version: v1.3.3-2dc9cb995 - OS: macOS - Version 15.0.1 **Additional context** Add any other context about the problem here. ```[tasklist] ### Tasks ```
gold_answer: The "Body exceeded 1mb limit" error comes from Next.js, not Inngest. Increase the max response body size for the Next.js API route, as described in the linked Stack Overflow answer, then retry.
gold_thread:
This looks similar to the report in #2016, but except for Next.js.

This error is from Next.js and not from Inngest, you can increase the max size of the max response body here.

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68574254/body-exceeded-1mb-limit-error-in-next-js-api-route

I will close this issue, please comment or re-open if this does not fix your issue with Inngest+Next.js

title: Dev Server Timeout
question: **Describe the bug** Dev server errors out with this error ```bash Error: read ETIMEDOUT at TLSWrap.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:217:20) at TLSWrap.callbackTrampoline (node:internal/async_hooks:130:17) ``` **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Restart you app 2. Restart inngest dev server 3. At times, recently very frequently inngest throws this error and then the second try is in limbo forever **Expected behavior** Dev Server should just work **Screenshots / Stack trace dump** **System info** - inngest-cli version: npx inngest-cli@latest - OS: macOS - Version 3.19.17
gold_answer: The ETIMEDOUT error is a Node.js socket timeout, most likely from your app's own step running too long or a downstream request timing out, not from the Inngest SDK. Check for slow or hanging external calls inside your steps.
gold_thread:
Hi there, this error that you see is a Node.js error which looks like your own app's timeout as your step is taking too long or is throwing this error, perhaps due to a downstream request that times out. 

Closing this as this error does not look like it's part of the SDK either. Thanks!

title: feat: Add support of waitForMultipleEvents
gold_answer: Use a small `waitForAny` helper that chains `.then` on each promise, resolves the outer promise with the first truthy result, and resolves `null` after `Promise.all` settles if none were truthy. Pass it `step.waitForEvent` calls for both events, each with its own timeout, e.g. `await waitForAny([step.waitForEvent(...), step.waitForEvent(...)])`.

title: [CLI] Add support for bun
question:
Hi, 

Is it possible to use CLI with the latest Bun version?

I tried running `bun x inngest-cli@latest dev` but it fails with the following error:

```bash
$ bun x inngest-cli@latest dev
error: Failed to run "inngest-cli" due to error InvalidExe
error: script "inngest" exited with code 1 (SIGHUP)
```

Thanks
gold_answer: Staff explained that `bun x` fails because inngest-cli relies on a postinstall script, which Bun only runs for packages listed in package.json `trustedDependencies`, and `bun x` offers no way to trust a package. Staff said there is no fix yet, that they are watching Bun's progress, and that they will look at alternatives if it takes a while.
gold_thread:
Thanks for the report, @piotrkulpinski, and the links, @osener.

I've been keeping an eye on this as had the same annoyance myself. 😁 There are a large number of affected packages that recommend `npx package@latest` (like Supabase in oven-sh/bun#4583 linked above) - we'll see where bun goes with the reports and look at alternatives if it's taking a while.
---
With the ecosystem's shift way from postinstall scripts and how pnpm has changed and npm will change, we are shifting away from using npm for the CLI distribution. We'll be shifting to direct bash installer or Homebrew.

title: [BUG] Next.js 15.5 mismatch types in API Route
question:
**Describe the bug**
Fails to build with latest Next.js 1.5 due to type changes in API Routes.

**To Reproduce**
```
import { init } from 'jobs'
import { functions } from './index'

// This is needed for making sure that the GET
// handler will never be statically generated
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'

export const { GET, POST, PUT } = serve({
    client: inngest,
    functions,
  })

```

```
...
Skipping linting
   Checking validity of types  ...Failed to compile.

Type error: Type 'typeof import("/Users/kostas/code/pblworks-monorepo/apps/admin/src/app/jobs/route")' does not satisfy the constraint 'RouteHandlerConfig<"/jobs">'.
  Types of property 'GET' are incompatible.
    Type 'RequestHandler' is not assignable to type '(request: NextRequest, context: { params: Promise<{}>; }) => void | Response | Promise<void | Response>'.
      Types of parameters 'expectedReq' and 'request' are incompatible.
        Property '[INTERNALS]' is missing in type 'import("/Users/kostas/code/pblworks-monorepo/apps/admin/node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/request").NextRequest' but required in type 'import("/Users/kostas/code/pblworks-monorepo/node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/request").NextRequest'.

Next.js build worker exited with code: 1 and signal: null
...
```

Temporary fix:

```
import { init } from 'jobs'
import { type NextRequest } from 'next/server'
import { functions } from './index'

type RequestHandler = (
  expectedReq: NextRequest,
  res: unknown
) => Promise<Response>

// This is needed for making sure that the GET
// handler will never be statically generated
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'

export const { GET, POST, PUT } = serve({
    client: inngest,
    functions,
  }) as RequestHandler & {
  GET: RequestHandler
  POST: RequestHandler
  PUT: RequestHandler
}
```

**Expected behavior**
Build passes

**Code snippets / Logs / Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**System info (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Mac
- Framework: Next.js 15.5
- Platform: Vercel

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.
gold_answer: The type error comes from two separate copies of Next.js resolving in the monorepo, one at the root and one in the admin app, so the NextRequest types don't match. Align the Next.js version between the app and the root, hoist dependencies so only one copy exists, or force a single version with resolutions/overrides.
gold_thread:
Thanks for the report, @kostas-pblworks!

Are you using any particular features of Next.js 15.5 that seemed to start causing this? Booting up a new repo for this, I'm struggling to reproduce it.

One thought is that the type mismatch stated looks like it's comparing two separate Next.js paths:

- `/Users/kostas/code/pblworks-monorepo/apps/admin/node_modules/next`
- `/Users/kostas/code/pblworks-monorepo/node_modules/next`

That would definitely be a cause for confusion if you have `next` installed at the monorepo's root as well as in your `admin` app.

Depending on hoisting settings in your repo and what package manager you're using, there would be a few paths to resolve this and make sure that your `admin` app and `inngest` resolve to the same Next.js:
- Align the versions of Next.js in the app and at the root
- Make sure that all deps are hoisted from the app, so there's no local vs root version, only root
- Use something like `resolutions` or `overrides` to force a particular Next.js version

If it's _not_ that, would you mind providing a small repro repo? 🙂 Or advising on which settings etc I can set to reproduce!

Hope this helps

title: [BUG] Update zod dependency version in inngest lib
question:
**Describe the bug**
Zod is listed as a dependency using `~3.22.3` in the inngest client library (it's at version 3.24.2 as of this bug report).

In a monorepo with other packages that list zod as a dependency or peer dependency but are less restrictive on the versioning, zod doesn't get hoisted and leads to version mismatch issues.

**To Reproduce**
1. Set up a monorepo with npm workspaces
2. `npm install inngest ai -w packages/my-package`
3. Create a tool, like:
```
import { tool } from "ai";
import { z } from "zod";

const weatherTool = tool({
  description: 'Get the weather in a location',
  parameters: z.object({
    location: z.string().describe('The location to get the weather for'),
  }),
  execute: async ({ location }) => ({
    location,
    temperature: 72 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 21) - 10,
  }),
});
```

**Expected behavior**
Typescript doesn't complain.

**Actual behavior**
Typescript emits the following error on `parameters`:
```
No overload matches this call.
  Overload 1 of 2, '(tool: Tool<ToolParameters, unknown> & { execute: (args: any, options: ToolExecutionOptions) => PromiseLike<unknown>; }): Tool<...> & { ...; }', gave the following error.
    Type 'ZodObject<{ location: ZodString; }, "strip", ZodTypeAny, { location: string; }, { location: string; }>' is not assignable to type 'ToolParameters'.
      Type 'ZodObject<{ location: ZodString; }, "strip", ZodTypeAny, { location: string; }, { location: string; }>' is missing the following properties from type 'ZodType<any, any, any>': "~standard", "~validate"ts(2769)
```

**Additional context**
I think either upgrading zod or switching `~` -> `^` the package.json would fix this
gold_answer: Inngest pins zod to ~3.22.3 because upgrading broke consumers who depend on older zod versions, and later zod versions dropped support for the TypeScript version Inngest supports, so the pin can't be lifted until Inngest v4. As a workaround, use npm `overrides` in package.json to force a single zod version across the monorepo.
gold_thread:
Ah, aye. Multiple versions of packages are super tricky. See https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/3429#issuecomment-2071816685. There are better ways of solving this a bit more delicately (see #924), but I don't think `zod` will be using those.

We're pinned to `~3.22.3` as we had the same issue in reverse; upgrading caused those importing an earlier version of Zod (due to any other library) to complain: 55a7485844d071ca7364a1380782025425da2062.

Additionally, later versions of Zod dropped support for the version of TypeScript that `inngest` supports, so upgrading would cause some consumer builds to break.

While that's something we'll be addressing in v4 (see #920), for now we can't upgrade without a break.

In the mean time, you should be able to use [`overrides`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v9/configuring-npm/package-json#overrides) to get back down to a single version.

title: [BUG] referenceFunction constructs a function-reference using '-'  instead of '/'
question:
**Describe the bug**
I am trying to use step.invoke to invoke a function within another service. For that I am using the appId and the function-name. I previously just used a full string and took the value from the local emulator as follows `<appId>/<fnName>`. After the deprecation notice I replaced it w/ referenceFunction, however, the constructed string is now `<appId>-<fnName>`. Inngest then fails with function not found (because of - instead of /)

**To Reproduce**
See above

**Expected behavior**
The generation of function-ids with app-ids should be consistent throughout the system
gold_answer: The fully qualified function ID is the app ID and function ID joined with `-` (slugified), so `referenceFunction` builds `<appId>-<fnId>`, not the `/` form shown in the Dev Server payload. The reporter's real problem was that the app and function IDs they passed didn't match how the target function was registered (it was registered as `jobs/<name>`), so the lookup failed.
gold_thread:
Hi @Figedi - are you using the TypeScript SDK? Under the hood, the fully qualified function id is the app id and the function id concatenated and slugified using `-`. I'm very curious how your previous use of a `/` character ever worked. Can you share your app id and function id/function name code here? You don't need to share any business logic, just the `Inngest()` client creation and the id/name used for `inngest.createFunction`. Thanks!
---
Glad you were able to get it sorted out @Figedi!

title: [BUG] Circular reference in middleware types
gold_answer: The circular reference error is a TypeScript bug fixed in TypeScript 5.1 (microsoft/TypeScript#52696), so upgrading TypeScript resolves it. If you need the run ID in function input, use the `runId` property passed to the createFunction handler.

title: [BUG] unhandled promise rejected on remix with vercel
gold_answer: The Remix/Vercel 'First parameter has member readable' error comes from web-streams-polyfill mismatches in the serverless runtime. Workaround: install @remix-run/web-fetch, pass its exported fetch into new Inngest({ id, fetch }), and remove allowStreaming: "force" from serve(). Staff also noted that event payloads must be JSON, so a Buffer in event data is not supported.
gold_thread:
Hi, @pullmann4rent! 👋

There have been a couple of reports of Remix having some issues with streams--or just generally around Node 18 compatibility and polyfills on Vercel--though this looks like it might be an issue trying to send a [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/buffer.html) in the event payload.

What is the type of `buffer` (the return of `await getPDFVerify()`)? We currently only accept JSON data in event payloads.
---

Hi @pullmann4rent!

Looks like the warning you're seeing is:

> Could not find an event key to send events; sending will throw unless an event key is added. Please pass one to the constructor, set the `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` environment variable, or use `inngest.setEventKey()` at runtime.

When calling `new Inngest()`, this warning is shown when the library can't detect an event key from the `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` environment variable. An event key is a unique key that allows your application to send (aka publish) events securely to Inngest.

Head to the [Creating an event key](https://www.inngest.com/docs/events/creating-an-event-key) docs to see how to get one and specify it in your app! 🙂

title: Support Vercel Edge Functions
question:
When using NextJS * Vercel Edge functions `fetch` is not correctly detected.

```
ReferenceError: XMLHttpRequest is not defined
```

Looking at the code https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/blob/main/src/components/Inngest.ts#L129 it looks like if you don't provide a fetch in the constructor it falls back to using cross-fetch, which I guess thinks the edge functions are a browser and tries to use XMLHttpRequest polyfil.

As a workaround supplying fetch seems to work and I'm able to send events.

```
new Inngest({fetch})
```
gold_answer: On Vercel Edge functions, the SDK's default fetch falls back to cross-fetch, which detects the edge runtime as a browser and fails with XMLHttpRequest is not defined. The workaround is to pass fetch explicitly, e.g. new Inngest({fetch}); staff said the SDK should bind to the global fetch automatically and that the client should be environment-agnostic, and they would open a PR for that.
gold_thread:
Hi @DaleLJefferson!

Great job for finding this. 🙌 We have #61 in the pipeline to support most edge environments generically (see [src/edge.ts:30](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/pull/61/files#diff-6d342bfccb89ad2031baad345fbc84ed2a1e624c070b3036a857ee88baf88de8R30) for that fetch binding), but this is exactly how to achieve this at present.

For this, we could probably try to bind to `fetch` if we find it as a global to avoid you having to do this manually.

#61 has a todo to add a Vercel edge function example - I'll venture to add this to [inngest/sdk-example-nextjs-vercel](https://github.com/inngest/sdk-example-nextjs-vercel) and then we can get this all sorted with tests.
---
Aye, the client should definitely be environment agnostic.

Will reference this with a PR to fix!

title: Can a scheduled function also be invoked as a standard event function?
question:
Can a scheduled function also be invoked as a standard event function?

I couldn't set cron and event in the same function definition.
gold_answer: Yes, a scheduled (cron) function can also be triggered by events. A function can have multiple triggers, but the first attempt failed because the config was set incorrectly. The fix is to declare both triggers in the trigger array, as described in the multiple-triggers guide.
gold_thread:
Yes, a scheduled function can be invoked as an event function. I was trying to set it wrongly.

Docs https://www.inngest.com/docs/guides/multiple-triggers

title: Does inngest support priority queue?
question:
My use case is to have free users and paid users for AI image generation service and I want paid users to frontrun free users when they enqueue their jobs.

I'm not super sure exactly about which data structure or algorithm I need but roughly I need to be able to rearrange the order of jobs based on user tier and their usage frequency somehow. Paid users will enjoy fast AI image generation and free users will not. Users on the same tier that use the service more often than others also should be deprioritized.
You can suggest me a solution. Thanks.
gold_answer: Yes, Inngest supports dynamic run priority: set a `priority` on the function that is computed from event data (for example, the user's tier), so runs for paid users can be prioritized over free users. See the run-priority docs for the expression syntax and how to use it.
gold_thread:
Yes, you can read our docs here: https://www.inngest.com/docs/reference/functions/run-priority.

This allows you to initialize function runs with dynamic priorities based off of event data.

title: Recommendations on waiting for a condition to happen
question:
I have a workflow that needs to hold on a specific step until some other processes update database records. I initially implemented this as a `RetryAfterError` to tell inngest to keep retrying however, as it's an "error", it then fails the entire workflow after the default number of retries.

What I want is for this step to execute every so often and only continue onto the next step once the database condition is met (which I could make work by pushing the allowed number of retries really high but that feels like a hack). What is the recommended way for implementing such logic? Should I make the step itself loop and sleep? Is the expectation that the other part of the app will emit a new event and I use `waitForEvent` here? I'm having a hard time finding answers to this in the docs.

Thanks!
gold_answer: Use `step.waitForEvent` instead of retrying with `RetryAfterError`. It pauses the function until a matching event arrives, and the `if` expression can match on an ID such as a completion ID. Have the other parts of the app emit that event when the database condition is met, which resumes the function.

title: Why are these throttled messages executing while earlier message has failed
question: I have this set of coordinated Inngest functions: https://github.com/cozemble/breezbook/blob/main/backend/airtable/src/inngest/announceChangesToAirtable.ts Their purpose is to push mutation events into airtable. You will notice that I try to limit any messages for a tenant and environment pair to 1, attempting to ensure the correct application order of the events (see https://github.com/cozemble/breezbook/blob/8949f2d5c2819b0597c6c54d9ff1cf3b451543b4/backend/airtable/src/inngest/announceChangesToAirtable.ts#L107) What I see when I run this locally, is that later events seem to get processed when an earlier event has failed. What do I have to do to ensure that later events wait if an earlier event has failed? Thx!
gold_answer: Inngest can block and retry a failed step until it succeeds or is dead-lettered. To enforce ordering, put the dependent operations in one function as sequential `step.run` calls, or have each function trigger the next one on completion instead of fanning out all events at once. Concurrency limits alone don't stop later events from running after an earlier one fails.

title: Clarity on code executed outside of steps
gold_answer: Code outside of steps re-runs on every function invocation until the next step is reached, so `getUser` at the top runs each time a step is invoked. Each step runs only once, and its output is stored in function state and injected on later runs. Code placed after the last step runs only once.
gold_thread:
It runs many times.  Steps run once and the first run's output is stored in function state and injected on the next run.

Code outside of steps is ran multiple times _up until_ we execute the next step.  For example, if this await was at the end of the function it only runs once, as it's not executed until all steps finish.  However, being at the top it's ran every time a step is invoked.

title: Steps in a for loops executes the steps to many times
question:
**Describe the bug**
Steps in a for loops executes the steps to many times

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
```tsx
const testInngest = inngest.createFunction(
  { id: "test-inngest" },
  { event: "test/many-steps" },
  async ({ event, step, runId }) => {
    for (let index = 0; index < 3; index++) {
      const random = Math.floor(Math.random() * 200);
      console.log(`index: ${index + 1} --|||-- random: ${random}`);
      await step.sleep("wait", random);
      await step.run(`plop ${index + 1}`, () => {
        console.log(`step plop ${index + 1}`);
      });
    }
  }
);
```

With this function, the logs are displayed too many times, example of the output:

```txt
index: 1 --|||-- random: 60
step plop 1
index: 1 --|||-- random: 90
index: 2 --|||-- random: 74
index: 1 --|||-- random: 49
index: 2 --|||-- random: 197
step plop 2
index: 1 --|||-- random: 46
index: 2 --|||-- random: 114
index: 3 --|||-- random: 157
index: 1 --|||-- random: 132
index: 2 --|||-- random: 46
index: 3 --|||-- random: 131
step plop 3
index: 1 --|||-- random: 35
index: 2 --|||-- random: 46
index: 3 --|||-- random: 51
```

**Expected behavior**
The output should me something like this:

```txt
index: 1 --|||-- random: 60
step plop 1
index: 1 --|||-- random: 49
step plop 2
index: 2 --|||-- random: 114
step plop 3
```

**Screenshots / Stack trace dump**
If applicable, add screenshots or paste what is output in your terminal to help explain your problem.

**System info**
- inngest-cli version: [e.g. 1.0.2]
- OS: [e.g. macOS]
- Version [e.g. 22]

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.
gold_answer: Inngest re-enters the function on every step, so each HTTP request runs one step and code outside steps re-executes each time, which duplicates console logs. Use the `logger` from the function input (e.g. `logger.info(...)`) to get logs that are returned reliably.
gold_thread: Hi @michaelchiche! What you're seeing here is how Inngest executes your function to ensure its durable and each part is safely retriable; Inngest re-enters your function for every step, meaning that roughly every HTTP request is intended to be running an individual step. You could also use the `logger` (available in function input, e.g. `async ({ event, step, runId, logger }) => { ...`) to get regular logs back. You can read more about how this execution works in [How Inngest functions are executed: Durable Execution - Inngest Documentation](https://www.inngest.com/docs/learn/how-functions-are-executed#how-steps-are-executed). --- Ah, aye this is intended to be demonstrating the exact confusion you're seeing: Should at least mention use of `logger` on this page though, 💯

title: Job fails when inngest cannot communicate with inngest API endpoint
question:
**Describe the bug**
We have long running jobs (> 2 hours) and we can see a pattern: these jobs always fail with this error:
```
Post "https://example.com/api/inngest?fnId=run-k6-test&stepId=step": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```
The error above is from the failure function:
```
    onFailure: async ({ error, event, step }) => {
      await step.run("update-test-status", async () => {
        console.log(error.message);
        ...
      });
      return;
    },
```
Also, the related function actually still runs after the failure function is triggered.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy NextJS and Inngest using a public domain
2. Start a long running jobs (2hours+)
3. Wait, or cause network disruption between inngest and the API server
4. Check if the job fails right away and the main function still executing

**Expected behavior**
- If inngest fails to communicate with the API endpoint, it should attempt to retry the requests several times, as network congestion can happen but that is temporarily, rather than failing the job right away

**Screenshots / Stack trace dump**
If applicable, add screenshots or paste what is output in your terminal to help explain your problem.

**System info**
- inngest-cli version: 1.4.5
- OS: ubuntu
- Version: 22.04

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.
gold_answer: The failure is expected: a single step has a hard 2-hour duration limit, which isn't configurable. Staff recommended splitting the job into checkpointed steps, and suggested k6's cloud offering for multi-hour tests if splitting isn't viable.
gold_thread:
Hi @danhngo-lx, the limit to the duration of a single step is 2 hours, so this timeout is expected ([docs](https://www.inngest.com/docs/usage-limits/inngest#timeout)).

To help you solve your issue, are you able to break up this 2 hour long step into multiple steps somehow? Generally for jobs that run for that long, it's also practical to break up the job into multiple steps which act as checkpoints to avoid any error late in the function's execution from requiring the entire function to restart from the beginning. 
---
Hi @danhngo-lx - this 2 hour timeout isn't configurable at this point in time and it's a non-trivial change for us to make in the foreseeable future.

Within the Inngest system, we need to keep a persistent HTTP connection open with your application which is a synchronous request in order to effectively catch failures and handle retries efficiently. This 2 hour timeout is baked deep into the system ensuring that the services that perform these outbound connections do not shut down prematurely if there is a up to 2 hour request being handled. While it is possible to change in our system, it can create a number of side effects that will have varying results.

There may be work arounds with our upcoming APIs that use outbound WebSocket connections instead of inbound HTTP requests, but these limitations are still baked in.

While I would love for Inngest to support 2+ hour steps, I do want to be honest with you and say that that won't happen in the near future. I do know that k6 has cloud operators that may be better suited with these multi-hour k6 tests.

title: Wait For Event if filtering broken
question:
**Describe the bug**
The wait for event function does not seem to be working. I can use the `match` filter, but not the if.

**To Reproduce**

I wait for an event that I send in another function. This does not work:
```
    await step.waitForEvent("embed-cards-finished", {
      timeout: "15m",
      event: "embed-cards-finished",
      if: `async.data.deliberationId == ${deliberationId}`,
    })
```

However, the match filter works:

```
    await step.waitForEvent("embed-cards-finished", {
      timeout: "15m",
      event: "embed-cards-finished",
      match: "data.deliberationId"
    })
```

**Expected behavior**
Match is supposed to be deprecated, and replaced with above.


**System info**
- inngest-cli version: 3.28.0
- OS: Mac OS 14.0 (23A344)
gold_answer: The `if` expression treats an unquoted interpolated value as a bare token, so string values must be wrapped in quotes inside the expression. Changing the expression to `async.data.deliberationId == '${deliberationId}'` fixes the filter, while `match` is the older alternative.
gold_thread:
Hi @Klingefjord , if the value of `deliberationId` is a string, you will need to encapsulate the string in the `if expression. See my modified code wrapping that with single quotes: 

```diff
await step.waitForEvent("embed-cards-finished", {
  timeout: "15m",
  event: "embed-cards-finished",
+  if: `async.data.deliberationId == '${deliberationId}'`, // see single quotes
-  if: `async.data.deliberationId == ${deliberationId}`,
})
```

Does this fix your issue?

title: step.run fails when data returned is too large
gold_answer: The PayloadTooLargeError comes from the user's own HTTP server body parser, not Inngest. For example, Express defaults to a 100kb limit, so raising it (e.g., express.json({ limit: '500kb' })) fixes it. Inngest's step output limit is 4MB.
gold_thread:
hi @lachlanmcmillan - What server framework are you using? The error that you shared looks like a server-error, which makes me believe that this is a configuration issue on your HTTP server. 

For example, if you're using Express, the default limit is 100kb ([docs](https://expressjs.com/id/resources/middleware/body-parser.html#:~:text=limit,Defaults%20to%20'100kb'%20.)), you would then have to increase your server's parsing size. 

```ts
app.use(express.json({ limit: '500kb' }));
```

This is highly dependent on your framework though so if you can share that, that's very helpful!

Inngest's step size limit is 4MB: https://www.inngest.com/docs/usage-limits/inngest#payload-size

title: `step.waitForEvent` does not get resolved if events are issued in quick succession
gold_answer: This is a known race condition: if the event arrives before `step.waitForEvent` runs, the wait never sees it and times out. There is no fix yet; a planned "lookback" feature, which depends on a new event database, will address it. Until then, workarounds are to delay the event or to handle the two events in separate functions.
gold_thread:
Hi everyone, this is an unfortunate race condition that can happen where the event is received prior to the `waitForEvent` being executed. 

We have a planned "lookback" feature that is not yet in development: https://roadmap.inngest.com/roadmap?id=f7ebedd6-3e37-4314-9897-5903ed1a7ba9 - you can upvote to stay updated on when that is released.

This feature will not be enabled until our new event database is in production which we haven't began work on yet. It may be a few weeks away depending on other projects timelines. This is an important issue that we're going to fix!

For now, there isn't a great workaround other than somehow delaying the event or handling the events in close proximity in separate functions.

title: [BUG] TypeError: Inngest is not a constructor при использовании версии 3.35.0
gold_answer: The user imported `createClient` from 'inngest' but called `new Inngest(...)`, so `Inngest` was never defined. The fix is to import the class instead: `import { Inngest } from 'inngest'`.

title: `transformInput` hang forever
gold_answer: Calling `ctx.step` methods directly inside `transformInput` hangs because it isn't a supported path. A workaround is to start the step call as a promise in `transformInput`, return it under a key in `ctx`, and `await` it in the function body before using the result. Staff noted that a dedicated hook for this kind of work may be considered in a later middleware version.

title: [BUG] @inngest/test hangs on step.sleep()
gold_answer: In @inngest/test, step.sleep() and step.waitForEvent() are not resolved automatically, so they must be mocked for the test to continue; an unmocked sleep hangs by design. The testing docs' Sleep and waitForEvent section covers how to mock them.
gold_thread:
Thanks for the report, @bradleyayers!

For `step.sleep()` and `step.waitForEvent()`, we currently expect that you mock them if you wish them to continue. This ensures you can easily test scenarios such as race conditions.

See [Testing - Sleep and waitForEvent - Inngest Documentation](https://www.inngest.com/docs/reference/testing#sleep-and-wait-for-event).

I'm interested to know if you'd still expect a default behaviour here. Perhaps `step.sleep()`'s default should be to immediately continue instead of hanging? Or perhaps display a warning when it hasn't been mocked?

title: Middleware should be provided to the serve function, not the client
question:
**Describe the bug**
As far as I can tell, middleware is only actually _executed_ during function runs, however we have to register them (globally, at least) in the client.

This is problematic if we need to use libraries which are not able to be imported in all the contexts that the inngest client might be used.

For example: `@appsignal/nodejs` is not able to be imported in the Next.js Edge runtime due to webpack issues, and we would like to be able to set tags and capture errors in functions using AppSignal. However, we also need to trigger functions using `inngest.send` in Edge functions and Next-Auth callbacks, which run in middleware (and therefore the Edge Runtime).

It would make sense to me (if my understanding is correct) that there's no reason the client needs to know about middleware at the point of triggering events, only at the point of running functions.

**To Reproduce**
1. Register a middleware in the inngest client which imports a non-webpackable client, like `import { setTags } from '@appsignal/nodejs'`
2. Call `inngest.send` from Next.js middleware
3. See various webpack errors trying to import the AppSignal server package

**Expected behavior**
I should be able to trigger events without having to import server only packages.

**Screenshots / Stack trace dump**
If applicable, add screenshots or paste what is output in your terminal to help explain your problem.

**System info**
- inngest-cli version: 0.23.0
- inngest 3.6.2
gold_answer: Middleware on the Inngest client also hooks into `inngest.send()`, so it is loaded wherever events are sent. Create a separate Inngest client for the restrictive edge environment that only sends events, without the server-only middleware. Keep the full client for `serve()` and function runs.
gold_thread:
Hi @samtgarson 👋

Thanks for reporting. I empathise with the annoyance here.

Middleware can also be used to hook into the lifecycle for sending events with `inngest.send()`, as well as affecting typing for functions. With that, a single piece of middleware can control almost all of the SDK's I/O, hence being placed on the client, but it's a tripwire nonetheless.

In your case, I'd recommend creating and importing a separate client for use in the edge environment for sending events, which gives you the chance to ensure only relevant middleware is used in the more restrictive edge environment.

I'll add a change to our docs to call out this workaround.

We're not 100% happy with the interaction between `new Inngest()` and `serve()`. We have some changes in the works, but I'll leave this issue open to confirm the workaround is valid for you and discuss what some improvements might be here.

title: Type errors in inngest types and in dependencies
question:
**Describe the bug**
Typescript (v4.4.3) gives type errors. The errors are both related to `inngest/types.d.ts` and Inngest's **type-fest** dependency module.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an instance of `Inngest`:
```typescript
import { Inngest } from "inngest";

const client = new Inngest({ name: "My app" });
```
2. Run `tsc`.

**Expected behavior**
I expected the code to be compiled without any errors.

**Code snippets / Logs / Screenshots**
**Temporarily fix**:
Setting typescript's `skipLibCheck` compiler option to true will solve the problem temporarily as it skips the type checking on imported packages. `tsconfig.json`:
```json.
  ...
  "compilerOptions": {
    "skipLibCheck": true,
  },
  ...
```

**Error logs:**
```sh
node_modules/inngest/node_modules/type-fest/source/camel-case.d.ts:25:32 - error TS1005: '?' expected.

25  infer FirstWord extends string,
                                  ~

node_modules/inngest/node_modules/type-fest/source/camel-case.d.ts:26:42 - error TS1005: '?' expected.

26  ...infer RemainingWords extends string[],
                                            ~

32    ...infer Rest extends ReadonlyArray<string | number>,
                                                          ~

137     tools: ReturnType<typeof createStepTools<TEvents, TTrigger>>[0];
                                                ~

174 };

Found 6 errors.

```

**System info:**

- OS: Mac
- npm package Version 1.5.1
- Framework Express
- Platform Netlify
gold_answer: The Inngest types use TypeScript 4.7 features (instantiation expressions), so TypeScript 4.4.3 is unsupported. Upgrade TypeScript to 4.7 or later; the minimum supported version was set to 4.7 in #151, and earlier versions may be supported in the future.
gold_thread:
Thank you for the report!

We must look into additional integration tests for different TS versions to root these problems out earlier.

Looks like `type-fest` shifted from supporting `>=4.2.4` to `>=4.7.0` in [v3.0.0](https://github.com/sindresorhus/type-fest/releases/tag/v3.0.0). The errors in our files should be resolved by providing some parenthesis around the `typeof` call.

A couple of actions from this:

- [ ] Be explicit about TS support via `peerDependencies` and  [`typesVersions`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/declaration-files/publishing.html#version-selection-with-typesversions)
- [ ] Add CI tests for specific TS versions to CI, used to fix existing issues documented above

Out of interest, @mahdavipanah, is there a reason you haven't upgraded past `4.4.3`?
---
Started looking at TS CI tests in #151.

We do make heavy use of [instantiation expressions](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-7.html#instantiation-expressions) that were released in [TS 4.7](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-7.html), so supporting earlier than that might include some lengthy rewrites. 🤔
---
@mahdavipanah We've set the minimum TypeScript version to `4.7` in #151.

We may be able to provide support for earlier versions in the future, though we use many of the large inference improvements made in 4.7 to provide good typing throughout the library.

Going to close as I haven't heard back in a bit, but please reach out if you'd like any help upgrading to 4.7+!
